source: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 10 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Write the unknown quotient and compare selected coefficients

hints.title: Write down the missing factor
hints.body: The degree is 4, and the given factor has degree 2, so the other factor is quadratic. Write it as Ax2+Bx+C.
hints.recap: The highest powers multiply to give the highest power of the product.
hints.pitfall: You do not need to find the roots of the given factor.
hints.pause: Compare the leading and constant terms to find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: The highest powers multiply to give the highest power of the product.

hints.title: Use the known cubic coefficient
hints.body: In the product of the two quadratic factors, collect just the terms containing x3. Their coefficient must be −11.
hints.recap: Equal polynomials have equal coefficients of each power.
hints.pitfall: For each power, include all products that contribute to it.
hints.pause: Find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>, then collect the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> terms to work out the requested sum.

recall.reminder: Equal polynomials have equal coefficients of each power.

solution:
1. The quotient must be quadratic. Its leading coefficient is 2, and its constant coefficient is 6, so write it as 2x2+px+6.

2. In (x2−4x+1)(2x2+px+6), the coefficient of x3 is p−8. Therefore p−8=−11 and p=−3.

3. The x2 coefficient is 6−4p+2=20, and the x coefficient is p−24=−27. Thus b+c=20−27=−7. Answer C.
